paragraphs.text: Πρὸ τούτων τῶν λόγων ἐλήμφθη Ἑνώχ, καὶ οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἔγνω ποῦ ἐλήμφθη, καὶ ποῦ ἐστιν, καὶ τί ἐγένετο αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: Pro toutōn tōn logōn elēmphthē Henōch, kai oudeis tōn anthrōpōn egnō pou elēmphthē, kai pou estin, kai ti egeneto autō.

i18n.en: Before these things, Enoch was taken; and none of mankind knew where he had been taken, or where he was, or what had become of him.

notes.official: Enoch the scribe-of-righteousness is taken — the foundational text of the **Enoch-as-mediator-figure tradition** that culminates in the Enoch-Metatron of 3 Enoch (Sefer Hekhalot). See central entry `enoch-as-scribe-mediator-figure-12-jub-4-metatron-cross-corpus` and existing v2.59.0 `metatron-shar-ha-panim-prince-of-the-presence-cross-corpus-hekhalot-hebrew-bible`. Cross-corpus to Gen 5:24 *wa-yithallēk Ḥănôk ʾeṯ-hā-ʾĕlōhîm wĕ-ʾēnennû kî lāqaḥ ʾōṯô ʾĕlōhîm* — the cryptic Hebrew Bible seed-text.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ αἱ ἡμέραι αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων ἐγένοντο, καὶ μετὰ τῶν Ἐγρηγόρων αἱ ἡμέραι αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai hai hēmerai autou meta tōn hagiōn egenonto, kai meta tōn Egrēgorōn hai hēmerai autou.

i18n.en: And his days were with the Holy Ones, and his days were with the Watchers.

paragraphs.text: Κἀγὼ Ἑνὼχ ἤμην εὐλογῶν τὸν κύριον τῆς μεγαλωσύνης καὶ τὸν βασιλέα τοῦ αἰῶνος, καὶ ἰδοὺ οἱ Ἐγρήγοροι τοῦ μεγάλου ἁγίου ἐκάλεσάν με Ἑνὼχ τὸν γραμματέα, καὶ εἶπόν μοι·
paragraphs.translit: Kagō Henōch ēmēn eulogōn ton kyrion tēs megalōsynēs kai ton basilea tou aiōnos, kai idou hoi Egrēgoroi tou megalou hagiou ekalesan me Henōch ton grammatea, kai eipon moi;

i18n.en: And I, Enoch, was blessing the Lord of majesty and the King of the age, and behold, the Watchers of the Great Holy One called me — Enoch the scribe — and they said to me:

paragraphs.text: Ἑνὼχ ὁ γραμματεὺς τῆς δικαιοσύνης, πορεύου καὶ εἰπὲ τοῖς Ἐγρηγόροις τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, οἵτινες κατέλιπον τὸν οὐρανὸν τὸν ὑψηλόν, τὸ ἁγίασμα τῆς στάσεως τοῦ αἰῶνος, καὶ μετὰ τῶν γυναικῶν ἐμιάνθησαν, καὶ ὥσπερ οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐποίησαν, καὶ ἔλαβον ἑαυτοῖς γυναῖκας, καὶ ἠφανίσθησαν μέγαν ἀφανισμὸν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς·
paragraphs.translit: Henōch ho grammateus tēs dikaiosynēs, poreuou kai eipe tois Egrēgorois tou ouranou, hoitines katelipon ton ouranon ton hypsēlon, to hagiasma tēs staseōs tou aiōnos, kai meta tōn gynaikōn emianthēsan, kai hōsper hoi huioi tōn anthrōpōn epoiēsan, kai elabon heautois gynaikas, kai ēphanisthēsan megan aphanismon epi tēs gēs;

i18n.en: Enoch, scribe of righteousness, go and say to the Watchers of heaven — who have abandoned the high heaven, the holy and eternal station, and have defiled themselves with women, and have done as the sons of men do, and have taken wives to themselves, and have wrought great corruption upon the earth:

notes.official: Enoch is dispatched by the Watcher-rebels to compose their petition for clemency — the **scribe-and-mediator** function. The role establishes the Enoch-figure as the intermediary between heaven and earth (between the throne-of-glory and the bound-Watchers) that the Hekhalot-Merkavah tradition develops into the Enoch-Metatron.

paragraphs.text: Ὅτι ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς οὐκ ἔσται αὐτοῖς εἰρήνη οὐδὲ ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν· οὐ γὰρ εὐφρανθήσονται ἐπὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Hoti epi tēs gēs ouk estai autois eirēnē oude aphesis hamartiōn; ou gar euphranthēsontai epi tois huiois autōn.

i18n.en: There shall be no peace for them upon the earth, nor any forgiveness of sins; for they shall not rejoice in their sons.

paragraphs.text: καὶ τὴν σφαγὴν τῶν ἀγαπητῶν αὐτῶν ὄψονται, καὶ ἐπὶ τῇ ἀπωλείᾳ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῶν στενάξουσιν, καὶ δεηθήσονται εἰς πάντα τὸν αἰῶνα, καὶ οὐκ ἔσται αὐτοῖς ἔλεος καὶ εἰρήνη.
paragraphs.translit: kai tēn sphagēn tōn agapētōn autōn opsontai, kai epi tē apōleia tōn huiōn autōn stenaxousin, kai deēthēsontai eis panta ton aiōna, kai ouk estai autois eleos kai eirēnē.

i18n.en: And the slaughter of their beloved ones they shall behold, and over the destruction of their sons they shall groan, and they shall make petition throughout the whole age, but there shall be no mercy and no peace for them.
